## Recognition of Country

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Recognition of homelands
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
homeland <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Culture_Homeland.csv")

# Data wrangling
homeland <- homeland %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(recognises_homelands_n:doesn_t_recognise_homelands_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(homeland_n   = recognises_homelands_n,
                nohomeland_n = doesn_t_recognise_homelands_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(homeland_n:nohomeland_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("homeland"),
                starts_with("nohomeland"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "homeland"   = "Yes",
                                              "nohomeland" = "No",
                                              "answered"   = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Yes",
                                           "No",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 68% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents aged 18 years and over living in Greater Melbourne reported that they recognised an area as their traditional Country. This equates to approximately 14,900 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Males and females were equally likely to recognise an area as their traditional Country (68% vs. 68%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following question was asked of all people aged 18 years and over completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

- Do you recognise an area as your homeland or traditional Country?
  - Yes
  - No

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

## Connection Through Returning to Country

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Frequency of visits to homelands
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
visit <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Culture_HomelandVisit.csv")

# Data wrangling
visit <- visit %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(several_times_per_year_n:never_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(several_n   = several_times_per_year_n,
                annual_n    = once_per_year_n,
                notannual_n = less_frequently_than_once_per_year_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(several_n:never_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("several"),
                starts_with("annual"),
                starts_with("notannual"),
                starts_with("never"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "several"   = "Multiple times per year",
                                              "annual"    = "Once per year",
                                              "notannual" = "Less than once per year",
                                              "never"     = "Never",
                                              "answered"  = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Multiple times per year",
                                           "Once per year",
                                           "Less than once per year",
                                           "Never",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 69% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents aged 18 years and over living in Greater Melbourne who recognised an area as their traditional Country do not currently live on their Country. This equates to approximately 10,300 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- 66% (approximately 6,800 people) of people who do not live on their traditional Country had visited, with 14% (approximately 1,400 people) visiting several times per year and a further 17% (approximately 1,800 people) visiting once per year.

- Females were more likely to visit their traditional Country several times per year than males (18% vs. 9.3%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following questions were asked of all people aged 18 years and over completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

- Do you recognise an area as your homeland or traditional Country?
  - Yes
  - No

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- If yes, do you currently live there?
  - Yes
  - No

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- If you do not currently live there, how often do you visit?
  - At least once a week
  - At least once a fortnight
  - At least once a month
  - Several times per year
  - Once per year
  - Less frequently than once per year
  - Never

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

```{r}
#
figure_count <- figure_count + 1

factor_levels <- stringr::str_wrap(levels(visit$answer), width = 15)

figure_number <- visit %>% 
  dplyr::filter(sex != "Total" & answer != "Total") %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(stringr::str_wrap(answer, width = 15), levels = factor_levels)) %>% 
  #
  f_bar_grouped_sex(x_variable = answer,
                    y_variable = n,
                    y_max      = NA,
                    y_breaks   = 250,
                    y_expand   = 160,
                    x_angle    = 90)

figure_percent <- visit %>% 
  dplyr::filter(sex != "Total" & answer != "Total") %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(stringr::str_wrap(answer, width = 15), levels = factor_levels)) %>% 
  #
  f_bar_grouped_sex(x_variable = answer,
                    y_variable = prop,
                    y_max      = 50,
                    y_breaks   = 5,
                    y_expand   = 0.5,
                    x_angle    = 90)

f_bar_grouped_combine(figure_number, figure_percent)
```

## First Nations Rights and Responsibilities for Lands and Waters

::: {.ctg-box}
**This topic aligns with [Closing the Gap Outcome Area 15](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/dashboard/outcome-area/land-and-waters/): Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people maintain a distinctive cultural, spiritual, physical, and economic relationship with their land and waters**

Target A: By 2030, a 15% increase in Australia’s land mass subject to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people’s legal rights or interests.

Target B: By 2030, a 15% increase in areas covered by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people’s legal rights or interests in the sea.
:::

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Land mass where native title exists
# Data from Native Title Determinations Outcomes
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Native Title data
nativetitle_land <- readxl::read_excel(file.path(root_folder, subfolder_ctg, "CTG15_Land_Waters_Data_Tables.xlsx"),
                                       skip  = 1,
                                       sheet = "Table CtG15A.1") %>% 
  janitor::clean_names() %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(model = x2,
                value = x3,
                type  = x4,
                year  = x5) %>%
  #
  tidyr::fill(model, value, type) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(model == "Actual" & type == "Total area") %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(vic)) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(value,
                year,
                vic)

# Data wrangling
nativetitle_land <- nativetitle_land %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(vic = as.numeric(vic),
                #
                value = dplyr::case_when(
                  value == "Land area" ~ "land_n",
                  TRUE ~ "land_prop")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from  = "value",
                     values_from = "vic") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(land_target_n    = 14934 + (14934 * 0.15),
                land_target_prop = 6.6 + (6.6 * 0.15))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sea area where native title exists
# Data from Native Title Determinations Outcomes
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Native Title data
nativetitle_sea <- readxl::read_excel(file.path(root_folder, subfolder_ctg, "CTG15_Land_Waters_Data_Tables.xlsx"),
                                      skip  = 1,
                                      sheet = "Table CtG15B.1") %>% 
  janitor::clean_names() %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(value = x3,
                type  = x4,
                year  = x5) %>%
  #
  tidyr::fill(value, type) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(value == "Actual") %>%
  dplyr::filter(year %in% c("2020", "2021", "2022", "2023", "2024")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(value = type,
                year,
                vic = vic_b)

# Data wrangling
nativetitle_sea <- nativetitle_sea %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(vic = as.numeric(vic),
                #
                value = dplyr::case_when(
                  value == "Sea area" ~ "sea_n",
                  TRUE ~ "sea_prop")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from  = "value",
                     values_from = "vic") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(sea_target_n    = 265 + (265 * 0.15),
                sea_target_prop = 2.6 + (2.6 * 0.15))

# Join land and sea data
native_title <- nativetitle_land %>% 
  dplyr::left_join(nativetitle_sea, by = "year")
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [Closing the Gap Information Repository](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/), compiled from the [National Native Title Tribunal Geospatial Data Model](https://www.nntt.gov.au/assistance/Geospatial/Pages/Spatial-aata.aspx).

- In 2024, 7.2% of Victoria’s land mass (approximately 16,351km^2^) was subject to Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people’s legal rights or interests, an increase from 6.6% (approximately 14,934km^2^) in 2020. This was below the Closing the Gap target of 7.6% (approximately 17,174km^2^).

- In 2024, 2.9% of Victoria’s sea area (approximately 295km^2^) was subject to Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people’s legal rights or interests, an increase from 2.6% (approximately 265km^2^) in 2020. This was below the Closing the Gap target of 3.0% (approximately 305km^2^).

- Detailed maps of areas covered by native title claimant applications, native title determinations, and Indigenous Land Use Agreements can be found on the [National Native Title Tribunal website](https://www.nntt.gov.au/assistance/Geospatial/Pages/Maps.aspx).

:::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Figure 7B-2

::: {#fig_7B_2 .fig-tab-title}
**Figure 7B-2:** Percentage of land mass and sea area subject to Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people's legal rights or interests on June 30th, by year
:::

```{r}
#
figure_count <- figure_count + 1

figure_percent <- native_title %>% 
  dplyr::select(year,
                land_prop,
                sea_prop) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols     = !year,
                      names_to = "prop") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(category = dplyr::recode(prop,
                                         "land_prop" = "Land mass",
                                         "sea_prop"  = "Sea area"),
                #
                hover_text = paste0(year, "\n",
                                    category, "\n",
                                    "Percentage: ", sprintf("%.1f", value))) %>%
  #
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = value, group = category, col = category, text = hover_text)) +
  #
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.5) +
  #
  geom_hline(data = native_title,
             aes(yintercept = land_target_prop),
             col       = colour_landmass,
             linetype  = "dashed",
             linewidth = 1) + 
  #
  geom_hline(data = native_title,
             aes(yintercept = sea_target_prop),
             col       = colour_seaarea,
             linetype  = "dashed",
             linewidth = 1) +
  #
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 10),
                     breaks = scales::breaks_width(1),
                     expand = expansion(add = c(0, 0.125)),
                     labels = scales::comma_format(big.mark = ",")) +
  #
  scale_color_manual(values = c(colour_landmass, colour_seaarea),
                     labels = c("Land mass", "Sea area"),
                     name   = NULL) +
  #
  labs(x = NULL,
       y = NULL) +
  #
  theme_classic()

figure_percent %>% 
  plotly::ggplotly(tooltip = "text") %>% 
  #
  plotly::layout(hovermode = "x",
                 #
                 yaxis = list(title = list(text     = "Percentage of land mass or sea area",
                                           font     = list(size = 13, family = "Arial"),
                                           standoff = 10)),
                 #
                 legend = list(x = 0.5,
                               #
                               orientation = "h",
                               xanchor     = "center"))
```

::: {.callout-note title="Data notes" icon=false collapse=false}
- Data were obtained from the [Closing the Gap Information Repository](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/), compiled from the [National Native Title Tribunal Geospatial Data Model](https://www.nntt.gov.au/assistance/Geospatial/Pages/Spatial-aata.aspx).
  - The Closing the Gap Information Repository brings together data from a wide range of data sources to provide up to date information for each Closing the Gap target, indicator, and contextual factors.
  - The National Native Title Tribunal Geospatial Data Model brings together information about native title claimant applications, native title determinations, Indigenous estates, registered and notified Indigenous Land Use Agreements, and registered native title bodies corporate.

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Total land mass, total sea area, and the percentage subject to Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people’s legal rights or interests are calculated based on jurisdictional boundaries sourced from [Geoscience Australia](https://www.ga.gov.au/scientific-topics/national-location-information/dimensions/area-of-australia-states-and-territories).

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Land mass subject to Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people’s legal rights or interests includes:
  - Determinations of native title (land subject to a determination that native title exists exclusive or non-exclusive)
  - Indigenous estates (land grants under various land rights regimes of the states and territories and the Commonwealth)

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- The Closing the Gap targets are marked with a dashed green line (land mass) and a dashed blue line (sea area) in Figure 7A-5.

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::
